fetch-depth: 0 on both CI jobs, and INVALID now means the packet is wrong rather than the checkout was thin. The check separates a commit absent from this clone (UNVERIFIED, and the run says it is not ancestry evidence) from one absent from this repository (INVALID); a shallow clone under CI is itself a failure naming the workflow line, so deleting fetch-depth: 0 goes red again rather than passing having checked nothing. Proven both ways on GitHub Actions: run 30754387170 is the first green verify since 2026-08-01, reaching [state] valid then tsc then 58 test files; run 30755347566 was then made red on purpose with a fabricated commit sha and failed with the single line 'MAR-464: merged/proven commit 0badc0ffee... is not a commit in this repository', not the shotgun every-issue-INVALID a shallow clone produced. The break was reverted at b977a8e. tests/state-check.test.ts builds throwaway repositories for all four cases including the shallow-in-CI guard.

The cause is accumulated store state, and the path is exact. Proof 3h ends by writing a snapshot dated observed_at + 120s, deliberately, and nothing removed it; putAgentDomState refuses any snapshot older than the newest the runner has said, so for two minutes afterwards the next run's seed was refused as out of order and every proof from 3c down ran against the previous run's world. The intermittency was a stopwatch, not a race. It is NOT decisionIdentity treating runs[].progress or current_step as a change, and not a second writer for synthetic-gmail-meeting-assistant; MAR-464's fix is intact and tests/snapshot-carryover.test.ts rules that hypothesis out rather than assuming it away. Proof 3 now forgets the agent before seeding, 3i takes the fabricated future back out, and 3b asserts the seed was stored rather than merely accepted - an out-of-order snapshot is declined as { ok: true, superseded: true }, so reading only ok let the step report success having written nothing. The rollback guard is untouched and the new test holds it to that. Evidence: three consecutive pnpm verify:shell runs, 56 proofs each, zero failures. Runs 2 and 3 seeded 29.6s apart (15:52:24.275Z and 15:52:53.863Z), so run 3 sat inside the 120s window that used to poison it and would have been superseded under the old code.

Found while proving MAR-466, not filed before this session. tests/broker-transport.test.ts failed 3 runs out of 3 under full-suite load on Windows, on master's own code with none of this branch's changes, and passed in isolation and on Linux CI. settle(400) bet a fixed sleep on Windows spawning a Node process; the failures read 'expected [] to have a length of 1' - the child had not written yet. It now waits for the line rather than assuming it, accumulating across drains because a drain is destructive. Assertions unchanged and lib/broker/ untouched. Fixed here because pnpm verify could not go green on Windows without it. Three consecutive full-suite runs: 59 files, 1032 passed, 8 skipped, zero failures.

The cause is arithmetic, not luck, and the job logs settled it the way MAR-466's store row did. Across all 13 CI runs since 2026-08-01, telemetry propagation is a constant 3.3-5.5s while the agent's fetch is bimodal: ~1s when all three sources answer, 11-16s when one does not (items_total 30 vs 20). agent-kit/template/agent.mjs reads sources sequentially with a 15s timeout each, and 6g had a single 20s budget covering the fetch AND the propagation behind it, so one hung source spent 15 of the 20 and left ~5 for a step needing ~4. On 0ac58ac the fetch took 15.6s and the telemetry 4.6s: the gate lost by 0.2s and reported it as '6g ...: null'. The blocked-fetch story and the did-not-finish-in-the-wait story are the same event from two ends. Fixed by serving the mandatory gate three loopback feeds, one per parser; live sources moved to advisory 6l, which is dated, names the source that failed and can never fail a release. Three defects fixed independent of root cause: 6g reported null and now reports what it waited for, how long, over how many polls and what it saw; 6i/6j/6k cascaded off `completed?.run_id ?? ""` into three misleading red lines and now skip explicitly; 6j asserted only that a verdict existed, which passes on a zero-item digest from three dead sources, and twice did exactly that (runs 30736386756 and 30753436632 carried 20 items where 30 were expected) - it now asserts grounded AND 9 of 9 cited. 6m enforces ADR 0004 by reading the source addresses back out of the digest DASH received and failing if any is off-machine. Evidence: hosted Windows runner slack went from 4.4s on the failing run to ~20s (digest in 265ms vs 15.6s); pnpm verify green on Windows; CI green on three separate pushes to PR #32, the last of which is docs-only, the same commit shape that originally failed. Known unrelated flake: tests/broker-transport.test.ts 'drops past its bound' failed once in 5 full-suite runs under Windows load and passes in isolation - MAR-472's file, a different test, not fixed here. See ADR 0004.

DASH-28. Nothing distinguished 'quietly working' from 'died and nobody noticed': every existing signal (telemetry, the 5s Agent DOM poll, process facts) was evidence of activity, never an expectation of it. Design decision: trigger.schedule is free text ('weekdays at 08:00 local time') with no parseable structure, so deriving an expectation from it would mean parsing prose unreliably - added one small additive field instead, trigger.expected_interval_seconds, optional and meaningful only alongside type:schedule; absent means no derivable expectation and the agent is never marked stalled. stalled is deliberately NOT part of AgentStatus (the wire vocabulary an agent/runner may assert) but a new WorkspaceStatus = AgentStatus | 'stalled', computed only in lib/workspace.ts's buildOverview from timestamps the state snapshot already carries (runs/tasks/audit_events) - no new storage, no new polling, no runner changes. The killed-vs-quiet distinction the issue asks for falls out for free: runner/state.ts's existing resolveStatus already turns a confirmed-dead process into offline/error before DASH ever sees the snapshot, and the new derivation never overrides offline, error, paused, needs_attention, or an agent with an active run; a manual-trigger agent is exempt by construction. Surfaced on the workspace page (status, status_detail, next_action, new last_activity_at fact) and, separately, on the work inbox page as a 'May need a look' section - not folded into InboxItem, which is built around an expires_at a stalled agent doesn't have. Tests use fixed Date instants throughout, not wall-clock sleeps. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 60 files / 1065 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed. pnpm verify NOT run - Electron processes were already running on this machine from the concurrent MAR-469 session, and DASH is single-instance by design (MAR-450), so the real shell smoke was skipped rather than risking a collision. Merged to master in PR #36 (b778b23) on 2026-08-03.

tests/broker-transport.test.ts > 'drops past its bound rather than queueing unboundedly' failed once in five full-suite Windows runs during MAR-473's session and passed in isolation - the same class of defect MAR-472 fixed elsewhere in this file, on the one test MAR-472 did not convert. settle(700) bet a fixed sleep on Windows spawning a Node process and getting 200 written lines through the pipe within 700ms; under load the drain sometimes read dropped === 0 because nothing had overflowed yet. Converted to the file's waitUntil helper, polling until dropped > 0, copying the two adjacent tests MAR-467's session had already converted. The drop count accumulates across polls because a drain is destructive (MAR-472's reason); the request count does not accumulate the same way and is read from the latest drain only - accumulating it produced a real local failure (65 > 64) from an early poll draining a not-yet-full buffer before a later, separately-bounded drain added its own count on top, which would have been a false failure of a bound the code never actually violated. Assertions unchanged. tests/ only; lib/broker/ and runner/ untouched. Evidence: three consecutive full-suite runs on Windows, each 60 files / 1056 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, plus a clean pnpm typecheck. pnpm verify was not run - not required for a tests-only change confined to this file. One CI run's shell-smoke check failed on an unrelated Windows EPERM cleanup race in a different proof's temp directory (dash-lapse-proof-*, part of MAR-467's work, nothing this branch touches); a rerun on the same commit passed clean, confirming it. PR open, not merged by this session.

ONE of the three cases is proven end to end and two are unit tests only; the split matters more than the total, and ADR 0005 records the judgment behind it. PROVEN END TO END on the installed shell (proof 8, using the issue's numbering): case 2, the request the runner destroyed because its bounded buffer was full. A real agent the runner spawned fired 200 brokered requests past a buffer of 64 and the shell's own broker loop drained, recorded and rendered them - 200 sent, 64 adjudicated, 136 dropped, identical in all three runs, so it is a bound being hit rather than a race. 8d is the load-bearing check: audit rows plus dropped requests may not exceed what the agent actually sent, which is exactly what a synthesised row would do, and a build that faked a plausible decision would pass every other check in the file and fail that one. 8e asserts the lapse carries no operation, decision or refusal; 8f asserts the rendered sentence names no operation either. UNIT TESTS ONLY: case 1 (DASH was closed) and case 3 (the answer DASH could not confirm was delivered). Case 3's runner half runs over the real local transport in tests/runner-server.test.ts and its DASH half - marking the right audit row - is in tests/broker-lapses.test.ts; what is not proven on the installed shell is the two halves meeting, because that needs a child to exit inside the window between DASH deciding and the runner writing. Case 1 cannot be driven by a proof running inside DASH, because it requires DASH not to be running; lib/broker/uptime.ts is tested exhaustively and the wiring in electron/main.ts is not covered by an installed proof. The issue's own account of case 3 was wrong and is corrected in ADR 0005: an undeliverable answer does not leave no trace, because lib/broker/execute.ts audits on every path before the answer travels, so the row already exists and overstates - it became a delivered column on the audit row rather than a second population of near-misses. The new broker_lapses table has no decision, refusal, operation, connection_id or request_id column and tests/store-sqlite.test.ts pins that list. Evidence: pnpm verify green on Windows at this tree - [state] valid, typecheck clean, 60 test files with 1056 passed and 8 skipped, and 63 installed-shell proof checks passed with zero failures plus one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release). Three smoke runs were triggered and the last two were green. The first failed 7d/7e/7f/7h/7i and the cause was inherited state, not this branch: a previous interrupted run had left its requests in the runner's bounded buffer, which survives DASH, and this pass drained them at startup (138 dropped, 64 undeliverable, both reported in the log), seeding the broker's per-agent replay set with proof 7's fixed request ids so this run's real calls came back duplicate_request. Proof 8 passed all six checks on that same first run. Proof 7's ids are now unique per smoke process, which is MAR-473's own lesson pointed the other way: a blocking gate that goes red for a reason unrelated to the change in hand teaches people to re-run it until it is green. See ADR 0005.

MERGED AND NOT PROVEN, and the distinction is the whole point: the attended harness and the runbook exist, and NOBODY HAS STOOD AT THE CONSENT SCREEN. A runbook is not a run, so this promotes nothing - MAR-458 and MAR-469 stay merged until a dated attended run passes. What was built: scripts/google-proof/main.ts (an Electron main entry, checks G0a-G16), scripts/prove-google.mjs (builds and launches it) and docs/real-google-proof-runbook.md. The design decision that mattered was NOT writing it as a standalone script driving lib/broker/ directly, which is the cheap way. It boots the same shell through the same electron/smoke-identity.ts and electron/main.ts, writes to the same user-data directory, uses the same OS vault, adopts the same runner and spawns a real child speaking the same broker protocol - so the only variable between it and proof 7 is which server answers, plus the pre-consent summary window, which is a renderer surface and not on the path any provider request takes. There is therefore no substrate seam between the two proofs, only one check. That check is 7n: proof 7's harness SERVES Gmail's two send endpoints and answers them with success, which is what makes 'DASH never called a send endpoint' a statement about DASH rather than about a provider's willingness to refuse. Google cannot be made willing, so G12b reads broker_audit instead and is weaker in exactly that way - it would not distinguish a request DASH built and Google rejected from one DASH never built. The asymmetry runs both ways and is why neither proof is redundant: G11 refuses both send attempts against a credential Google would genuinely have honoured, which no loopback grant can model because that grant is a fixture the harness wrote itself. Both stay; proof 7 runs on every commit and this one runs when somebody is watching. G0b is the cheapest check and the one the whole record rests on - loopbackProofOrigin() must be null, or every check below would pass against the fake provider and the dated log would be a lie about which server answered; the run stops there if it fails. It cannot become a gate by construction, not by convention: scripts/prove-google.mjs exits before it builds anything if CI is set or no terminal is attached, and no package.json script names it (ADR 0004). pnpm verify does not run it and DOES typecheck it - tsconfig.json now includes scripts/google-proof - because a proof that rots silently between attended runs would be worse than none, and typechecking a file is not executing it. The write half creates a REAL draft in a REAL Drafts folder, said before the step and behind a typed confirmation; DASH has no operation that deletes a draft and this proof must not be the reason one gets built, so the operator deletes it in Gmail and confirms. The run ends by revoking at Google, which is also check G15b: the agent's next request must come back 'revoked' rather than as a generic failure, a MAR-446 acceptance criterion that until now had only ever been asked of a test server returning a hand-written invalid_grant. Regime when it is run: Testing mode with a named test user. Both scopes are RESTRICTED, a public connection needs Google verification, and restricted-scope data crossing a server needs an annual CASA assessment - none of which a Testing-mode run is evidence about. Testing-mode data-scope grants expire SEVEN DAYS after issue, so the record must carry its date. Evidence for this session, and it is evidence about the HARNESS rather than about Google - the attended proof itself is unexecuted: two full pnpm verify runs on Windows, both green, and the requirement they were run against is that verify still passes WITHOUT this proof in it. Each reported [state] valid with the 6 recorded drift warnings, typecheck clean, 62 test files / 1113 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, and 67 installed-shell proof checks with ZERO failures plus the one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release; all three answered, 456-604ms). 67 is unchanged from c6c3406 and that is correct: MAR-421 landed in between and added 9 unit tests and no installed proof, which is why the test count moved from 1104 to 1113 and the proof count did not. What varied between the two runs was the harness and not the product, and the first account of it written here was wrong in a way worth recording. Run 1's exit code did not appear when the run finished, because the smoke leaves the runner running on purpose and that detached process inherits the Tee-Object pipeline's stdout handle, which PowerShell waits on - so the pipeline stayed open with the log complete and locked. That was recorded as an exit code that was never observable, and it was DELAYED rather than lost: run 1 reported VERIFY_EXIT=0 about twenty minutes later, when the runner exited and released the handle. Both runs are therefore exit 0. Run 2 had already been launched through cmd.exe with file redirection, which waits on the child rather than on its grandchildren and recorded exit 0 immediately, and it ADOPTED run 1's runner (pid 40672) rather than starting a new one, which is the designed path. The runner was never stopped to force the issue: it may sit in that process tree and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing it. Separately, and this is as far as an unattended session can validate a proof that requires a consent screen: scripts/google-proof/main.ts is confirmed present in the typecheck program via tsc --listFilesOnly, esbuild bundles the entry cleanly, and the generated agent script was extracted from its template and passed node --check - the escaping bug proof 7 records as costing it several three-minute cycles, ruled out before the first attended run rather than during it. One real defect was found by reading the harness back rather than by running it, and fixed in f64a283: a run that died after G2 would have deleted DASH's copy of a live restricted-scope grant while leaving the grant itself alive at Google for the rest of its seven days, owned by a throwaway proof agent and invisible from DASH - the exact orphan lib/connection-actions.ts refuses to create when a disconnect half-fails, reintroduced by a proof. Revocation now happens on every path and before the vault delete, and the draft id is printed on every path too. See ADR 0002 amendment 3 for what a green run may promote, and the runbook's promotion rule for the four qualifications each promoted note must carry.

ADR 0002 stage 2: gmail.draft.create writes a reply into the user's own Drafts folder, and there is still no send operation. PROVEN END TO END on the installed shell (proof 7, checks 7k-7n): a real agent the runner spawned drove a real POST carrying a real bearer token to a real HTTP provider, and the RFC 5322 message DASH composed was read back out of what the provider received. 7n is the load-bearing check - the harness SERVES Gmail's two send endpoints and answers them with success, so 'DASH never called a send endpoint' is a statement about DASH rather than about a provider's willingness to refuse; over a run in which the agent asked to send twice by two different names, the paths DASH actually reached were /token, the two read paths and /gmail/v1/users/me/drafts. 7l reads the composed headers back and asserts no From, no Bcc and nothing the agent named; 7m shows a recipient carrying CRLF refused as invalid_input before any request, with exactly one draft POST in the whole run. NOT PROVEN, and unchanged from MAR-458: the provider is a loopback server, not Google. Nothing here is proven against Gmail's API - including that a draft appears in a real Drafts folder - and MAR-468 owns that. UNIT TESTS ONLY: the durable replay memory meeting a real DASH restart. hasBrokerRequest is tested against a real store in tests/broker-write.test.ts and the broker's use of it is tested with two brokers sharing one record, which is what a restart looks like from the broker's side, but no installed proof restarts DASH between two halves of one agent's work. What replaced stage 1's free argument: stage 1 could say 'no send exists' because nothing was built on gmail.compose, and that is spent. A write operation now has no plan - it cannot return a URL, a path or a method because WriteOperation declares no member that could carry one - so planCall builds a POST's URL from the operation's own frozen path, checked at module load against WRITE_PATHS, which tests/broker-threat-model.test.ts pins by value. There is no raw input: DASH composes the message from four typed fields and writes no From, so Gmail fills the sender from the account whose token DASH presented. Honesty changes that were not optional: Google has no drafts-only scope, so the disclosure that used to ride on unused_scopes would have vanished the moment something was built on compose - wider_permission and consequence are now required fields on a write operation and render before a sign-in as well as after. draft.placement is a required tagged union because the draft artifact kind stopped meaning local; it is the agent's claim and broker_audit is DASH's record, which the copy says. Evidence: six executed pnpm verify runs on Windows, all six green - [state] valid, typecheck clean, 61 test files, and 67 installed-shell proof checks with zero failures plus the one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release; arXiv timed out on one run and correctly did not affect the verdict). The first four ran at 1095 tests; master was merged in twice as MAR-441 and then MAR-474 landed, and the last two both report 1104 - MAR-441 added nine tests and MAR-474 repaired an existing one rather than adding any. The final run is on the merge commit actually under review. Proof check count went 63 -> 67 with 7k, 7l, 7m and 7n, and proof 8 reported the same 200 sent / 64 adjudicated / 136 dropped in every run. Five runs were triggered and one never executed: its Tee-Object could not open a log file an earlier run still held, which killed the pipeline before pnpm started, so it produced no output rather than a failure. Run 1's exit code was also lost on the harness side, to a truncating PowerShell pipeline rather than to anything in the run; every later run recorded exit 0, including the last one, which ran on the merge commit that is actually being reviewed. Neither harness fault touched the product. Merged to master in PR #35 (merge commit c6c3406) on 2026-08-03; the note this replaces called that PR open and human-gated, which was true when it was written. Still merged and not proven for the same reason MAR-458 is: MAR-468's attended harness and runbook exist and have not been executed. See ADR 0002 amendments 2 and 3.

The permission broker's first slice. Raw access-token delivery is closed: deliverableSecretFields cannot return an OAuth target and assertNoBrokeredCredentials refuses the spawn if one appears. An agent invokes gmail.search and gmail.message.read, whose provider URL DASH constructs and whose response DASH projects, and writes a LOCAL draft artifact; no send operation and no provider-side draft creation exist, so gmail.compose grants nothing. A grant is the intersection of what DASH implements, what the manifest declared and what the provider issued, re-resolved on every call so a disconnect binds at the agent's next request. Not proven: the installed proof runs against a loopback provider because Google needs an account, a human at a consent screen and a restricted-scope verification DASH does not have, so proof 7 establishes the boundary and not Gmail's API. Also not done: the compiled Google client id is disclosed on the capability card rather than removed, and BYO-client onboarding stays where ADR 0002's rollout puts it. See ADR 0002 amendment 1, which corrects this ADR's own account of the defect. Still merged as of 2026-08-03: MAR-468 built the attended harness and runbook that would promote this and has not been executed, so nothing about Gmail's API is claimed here yet. ADR 0002 amendment 3 records what a green attended run would make true, and the four qualifications this note would then have to carry.

DASH-17's first delivery slice: in-app/system popup on the existing DASH-13 command envelope. Chief chat (blocked on MAR-419) and every external channel stay unbuilt, per the issue's own ordering. Two new surfaces watch the same cross-agent work inbox app/work/page.tsx already reads: an OS Notification the moment a runner-enforced approval first appears, and an always-on-top popup window shown while any approval is pending and hidden the instant none is. Neither is a second command path: the popup's window is given the app's ordinary preload.js (not credential-prompt.ts's bespoke, command-incapable one, which exists for the opposite reason), so its Approve/Reject buttons call submitAgentCommand exactly as app/agents/detail/page.tsx does, reaching the one audited IPC channel every window shares. Resolving the same request from two surfaces exactly once, and refusing-and-auditing an expired one, needed no new logic: both already fall out of lib/agent-dom/runner.ts's existing idempotency key and enforceCommand. New code is intentionally thin: lib/shell/approval-popup.ts (pure, unit tested) decides which work-inbox rows count as a live, notification-worthy approval; electron/approval-notifier.ts and electron/approval-popup.ts are wiring, per this directory's own convention untested by vitest. lib/broker/ and runner/ untouched. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test (native PowerShell, to dodge Git Bash's whoami shadowing the Windows one 5 unrelated channel-secret.test.ts cases depend on) 61 files / 1074 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, including 9 new cases; pnpm state:check valid. The popup route was manually checked in a browser tab against a throwaway dev server: renders its read-only fallback cleanly, no console errors - a browser tab cannot exercise the installed-shell path (a real notification, a real popup window), which is what pnpm verify's Windows shell smoke is for. ADR 0006 decides that the broker's reach ends at the machine DASH is installed on: a process DASH's own runner did not spawn gets no brokered credential, DASH will not operate a hosted token broker, and an agent that must run while DASH is closed holds its own credentials on the agent_managed path that already exists. That is option 3 for the broker and option 1 for the product, argued as one rule about one boundary rather than two decisions. THE FINDING THAT SHAPED IT: the rule is already enforced by the transport rather than by policy. Since MAR-430 the runner listens on a Unix socket or a Windows named pipe and never on a port, so there is no address an off-machine process could dial, and runner/server.ts keeps isLocalPeer only against a TCP listener that does not exist. What was missing is that nothing writes it down - which is why examples/gmail-meeting-assistant.manifest.v2.example.json can declare continues_when_dash_closed true beside two dash_managed connections, validate, and tell the user only afterwards as an ADR 0005 case-1 lapse row. A hosted broker was rejected on four costs and the shortest decides it: it would make ADR 0002 invariant 1 a rule again after amendment 1 spent a paragraph on why its being a FACT about where the code can run is what made the boundary worth having. The other three: what a user trusts changes category from installed software to an operator; revocation stops being locally checkable, which is proof 7n's lesson pointed at a receipt; and ADR 0002's own Google release path attaches an annual independent CASA assessment at an assessor-set fee the moment restricted-scope data crosses a server. Its receipt already fails the honesty test IN THE CODE: describeCustody's hosted_broker sentence is missing the clause its remote_mcp_server sibling has, and both ways of writing it are bad. ON THE CONTRACT QUESTION: continues_when_dash_closed is NOT sufficient and NO new field is needed. It asks a question about time where a grant needs one about place, and the shipped Gmail example disproves it directly - runtime.class local_process, locations.runtime.kind local, continues_when_dash_closed true. locations.runtime.kind already carries place, is required, and orchestratekit-mcp already emits it (runtimeLocationKind maps managed_worker/scheduled_job/workflow_platform to remote); it must not be the gate either, because it is the author's claim about a fact DASH observes directly by having spawned the process. So it drives copy, never a grant. ADR 0002 amendment 4 narrows the four sentences of 0002 that were written as universals - the Decision's first line and invariants 1, 3 and 5 - and records that invariant 6 keeps every word while stopping being reassuring about the mailbox. PLANNED and deliberately without a commit: PR #44 is open and human-gated, so nothing here is on master and no ancestry is claimed. Filed AFTER the fix rather than before it - the work arrived as a bug report against MAR-420 on master - and an issue written afterwards is a record rather than intent, which is why it says so. MAR-420's DensityScript sets data-density on document.documentElement before hydration, and app/layout.tsx renders <html>, so React hydrated it, found an attribute the build-time markup never had, and logged a mismatch on every load. The comment beside the script asserted the opposite - 'suppressHydrationWarning is not needed: this touches <html>'s attribute, not any element React rendered' - and the running app had been disproving it since #42 merged. Fix is <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning> plus the comment rewritten to say what is true. The alternative was checked first and is unavailable: rendering data-density server-side needs a server, and the packaged renderer is output: export built on a machine that has never met the user; dropping the script brings back the flash it exists to prevent. The flag works one level deep, so it covers <html>'s own attributes and nothing inside <head> or <body>. WHAT IT COST, honestly: the console and only the console. Production hydration does not warn and React patches no attribute either way, so compact kept working and nothing on screen was wrong - which is also why every gate here was blind to it. It is a dev-mode message, no test reads a console, and the three density proofs from the MAR-440/MAR-420 pass photograph a fresh window by clicking the real control, a window with no stored preference to disagree about. It is every load only for a user who has CHOSEN compact; with the default stored the script writes nothing. Two regression tests in tests/density.test.ts: the flag must be on the <html> app/layout.tsx renders, and it must appear on exactly ONE element in app/ - it turns off a real check, so spreading it is how a genuine mismatch elsewhere stops being reported. Both were confirmed red with the fix reverted and green with it back, which is MAR-465's rule applied to a unit test. Their first draft failed against prose - /<html\b[^>]*>/ matched a backticked <html> in a comment and the file that only DESCRIBES the flag was counted as carrying it - so the scans strip comments now; that is the same confusion between a comment and the thing it describes that caused the defect. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 65 files / 1204 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed (1202 before, these two); pnpm state:check valid with the same 7 recorded drift warnings; and next dev with dash.density=compact stored giving a clean console on / and /runs/detail across fresh loads, the attribute still applied, --density-row-y still 4px and the toggle still flipping both attribute and storage. pnpm verify:shell was not run LOCALLY - Electron was running from the main checkout and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing it - but CI's Windows shell-smoke job ran it on the branch tip b26107b and it passed: 70 proofs, zero failures, plus the advisory 6l with all three live sources answering. 70 is unchanged from the MAR-440/MAR-420 pass and that is the right number: this change adds no installed proof, and a count that moved would mean it had touched the installed loop. So the gap in the local evidence was closed by the gate rather than argued away, which is the better outcome and was not this session's doing.
